meta.title: When Teachers Become Students · EduFest 2026
meta.description: Workshop 4 at EduFest 2026, RMIT University Vietnam (SGS), 5 December 2026. Take an agentic AI class as a student, then flip to the teacher seat. 90 minutes, 50 seats.

place.venueName: RMIT University Vietnam, Saigon South (SGS) Campus, Building 2

hero.title: When Teachers Become Students
hero.titleAccent: Step Inside the Agentic AI Classroom
hero.subtitle: For 90 minutes, take an agentic AI class as a student on your own phone or laptop, then flip to the teacher seat to see how it was built. The lesson is AI-native teaching 101: AI that helps students learn rather than answer for them.
hero.venueValue: RMIT University Vietnam, Saigon South (SGS) Campus, 702 Nguyen Van Linh, Building 2
hero.stageLabel: An illustrated live class: you sit in a student seat while the AI agent answers with a hint, not the answer.
stageBullets: Ask a question back before answering
Give the next hint, never the answer
Let the teacher switch AI off
hero.stageTyping: Can you just give me the answer to question 3?
hero.stageReply: What does the question ask you to find first? Start there, and I'll give the next hint.

agenda.title: Run of show
agenda.subtitle: From a traditional setup to a cloud- and AI-native classroom. Upskii before class, Meet in class, Tasks after.

s0.title: Doors: sign in as a student
s0.body: Scan the QR code or open the short link, then sign in to Upskii with Google or Microsoft. Floor helpers and backup cards cover Wi-Fi and sign-in.

s1.title: Today you are the students
s1.body: A traditional classroom in 60 seconds next to an agentic one, and what the room will try in the next 90 minutes.

s2.title: In the student seat
s2.body: Join the class by link, read Hints, not answers, ask the AI tutor (hints only), take the five-question AI quiz and explain your class AI rule to the English coach.

s3.title: Flip to the teacher seat
s3.body: How the class was built: AI lessons from a five-line outline, live; AI-generated assessments; the results of the quiz you just took; the invite link.

s4.title: The class moves live
s4.body: Settings → Integrations shows Upskii linked to Tuturuuu, and starting the live class opens Meet. Everyone joins from the same link, guests included, and chooses at join whether Mira takes part.

s5.title: A live agentic classroom
s5.body: The responsible-AI lesson from Upskii with Follow me, a poll, a three-minute pair-talk timer, a whiteboard and the Upskii quiz in Quiz Arena. Q&A, transcript and notes run throughout.

s6.title: Q&A, still live
s6.body: The meeting stays open while the moderator brings up the top-voted questions from Meet Q&A.

s7.title: After class
s7.body: End the meeting: AI notes become action items on the class project board, each linked back to the meeting, with what changed since last time. Keep the class, your quiz result and your lesson-plan task.

tools.title: Who runs the session
tools.subtitle: Two speakers lead the session; the teams that build Tuturuuu and Upskii run the floor and the live demos.
tools.tuturuuuBlurb: The workspace for live classes, AI agents, notes, tasks and the calendar used throughout the session.
tools.upskiiBlurb: AI-assisted courses, quizzes and assessments. You build and take a lesson here.

who.a: Teachers, teaching assistants and school leaders who want to see what AI can do in a real lesson. There are 50 seats.

skills.a: No. If you can join a video call on a phone or laptop, you can take part. Everything is guided.

ready.q: Is everything shown ready to use?
ready.a: Not all of it. Each item is labelled Live, In progress or Planned from the public roadmap, and demos that are not public yet say Coming. Planned means not built yet.

answers.q: Will the AI simply give students the answers?
answers.a: In this workshop the assistant gives hints only. Teacher controls for each class (off, hints only or full help) are planned, and AI assistants in Meet are off by default.

data.a: AI assistants in Meet are off by default and switched on per workspace. Mira's memory is kept per person and per workspace, never shared across schools. AI in live rooms needs an audience confirmed as 18+, so it is not for younger classes yet.

registration.a: Registration is not open yet. Seats are limited to 50, and registration details will be announced here.

after.a: You leave with a plan for one lesson, using the capabilities that are live today.

classroom.title: What changes in an AI-native lesson
classroom.body: Prepare, practise, give feedback and follow up: the same lesson, run the traditional way and the AI-native way.

assistant.title: Hints, not answers
assistant.body: Use AI as a tutor: questions back, hint ladders, and when to switch AI off.

assess.title: Assessment that still measures learning
assess.body: AI drafts the questions, you review them, and the process is graded as well as the product.

responsible.title: Responsible AI in your class
responsible.body: Consent, the 18+ rule and minors, where data lives, and what to tell parents.

demos.title: Live demos
demos.subtitle: Live demos run on real products; previews not yet public are marked Coming. Each card says how ready it is today.

classroom.title: A live classroom on Tuturuuu Meet
classroom.body: Live on Meet today: screen sharing, host approval to join, forms in the call and team quizzes whose answers stay hidden until the reveal. Video adapts to the connection, and Data saver lowers quality on a weak one. Classroom mode, with class-size caps, co-teachers and shared class materials, is in progress, and rooms for up to 100 people are a target; hosted video capacity is not yet verified.
classroom.try: joining from your phone and answering a live poll.

mira.title: Mira, the AI assistant
mira.body: An AI assistant for students and teachers that remembers context for each person and workspace. Mira is coming to Zalo and Discord chats. In a live room it needs an eligible workspace and an audience confirmed as 18+.
mira.try: asking Mira for a hint, not the answer.

lms.title: Teach and Learn
lms.body: One learning platform: Teach for building quizzes, grading and attendance; Learn for practice and progress. Practice quizzes show results right away; graded tests keep answers hidden until scores are published. Flashcards are coming.
lms.try: taking a practice quiz, then seeing the teacher's grading view.

booth.title: The EduFest booth game
booth.body: A preview of a walkable 3D booth fair where each visitor signs in with Google (or a Tuturuuu work account) and casts one vote, with live results for organisers.
booth.try: a first look at the fair and how voting works, if it is ready on the day.

fleet.title: The agent team behind it
fleet.body: Tuturuuu is built by many AI agents working across machines, with people reviewing and approving every sensitive change.
fleet.try: watching agents plan, build and hand work to a person for approval.

edge.title: Built on the edge
edge.body: Meet's video and live rooms run on Cloudflare's global network, and more of Tuturuuu is moving there to keep pages fast and running costs down.
edge.try: seeing where a class's video is served from.

liveClass.title: Try the live class
liveClass.subtitle: Three moments from the session. Ask for help, play the team quiz, then swap to the teacher's seat.

ask.workshopNote: The workshop runs on hints only. Teacher controls for each class:

equation.hint: What could you do to both sides to leave 2x on its own? Try that first.
equation.answer: Subtract 6 from both sides: 2x = 8. Divide both sides by 2: x = 4.

loop.q: My loop never stops. What did I miss?
loop.hint: Look at the line that changes your counter. Does it ever reach the value that stops the loop?
loop.answer: The counter never increases. Add count = count + 1 inside the loop and it stops after 10 runs.

quiz.question: Team quiz: 2x + 6 = 14. What is x?
quiz.pickPrompt: Pick your team's answer, then lock it in.
quiz.locked: Locked in. Answers stay hidden until the teacher reveals them.
quiz.right: Correct. Your team earns a point.

seats.label: Your seat
seats.studentBody: You learn something new on your own device, ask for hints when stuck and answer the quiz with your team.

stuck.step2: Moving terms to the other side

agentTeam.title: The agent team behind the tools
agentTeam.subtitle: One example of how a change reaches you: people ask and approve, and AI agents help plan, build and check the work in between.

request.title: Request
request.body: A person describes what is needed.

plan.title: Plan
plan.body: An orchestrator agent splits the work into parallel lanes.

build.title: Build
build.body: Builder agents work at the same time on several machines, each in its own copy of the code.

review.title: Review
review.body: Agents help review the change and run the checks. Sensitive areas also need a person's review.

approve.title: Approve
approve.body: People approve sensitive changes, such as sign-in, billing and infrastructure.

ship.title: Ship
ship.body: The change reaches the main branch and is released once its checks pass.
